interpretation: Collapse at35-37C followed by faster operation at37-39C weakens a simple temperature-threshold explanation. Composite temperature and unavailable internal counters cannot exclude every thermal mechanism. Pause recovery is consistent with queue drain or device housekeeping, not proof of SLC cache exhaustion. Lifetime catchup pacing inflates early post-pause rate.
No prolonged collapse; isolated long writes remain. File size8GiB confounds comparison with mixed16GiB; next trial matches16GiB. No-catchup pacing prevents post-pause rate debt.

Fast through roughly250s wall time, then final~20s slower. File size alone not excluded; sequential writes can also slow without two writers, but the late transition requires repeat/control. No-catchup pacer.

All six phases fast with no>20ms sampled writes. Simple1GiB versus16GiB active-range threshold does not explain the mixed workload collapse. Both this test and earlier mixed data-only bypass differ in WAL caching and writer count; next test bypasses both files.

8KiB offset adds kernel-copy fallback and read amplification with repeated median-latency increases; long stalls appeared in second shifted phase and persisted into final aligned phase. Alignment overhead established, sole attribution of prolonged collapse is not. Next same-file F_NOCACHE toggle holds alignment fixed.

Long stalls do not cleanly follow current cache flag: they arise in no-cache third phase after cached second phase and persist across subsequent phases. Static A/B/A cache comparisons are not sufficient to establish a universal cache cure or sole root cause. Need kernel stack trace to separate pending storage I/O from software throttling/queueing. Effective state query denied2, spindump without root denied77, sudo -n requires password.

result.health_limitations: SMART composite temperature only; unavailable controller thermal and internal NAND counters prevent ruling out every internal thermal or firmware mechanism. Driver timing includes queueing, alignment and transfer, excludes separate flush operations. Windows use nearest observed endpoints; pause boundaries can straddle intervals.
result.limitations: Per-process counters omit inaccessible processes and activity between final observation and process exit. Sample latency maxima omit the last partial interval. Buffered writes, file reuse, and fsync cadence approximate components, not a complete PostgreSQL workload.

limitations: One aligned 1 MiB O_DSYNC writer, preallocated 16 GiB overwrite range; not a mixed database or arbitrary SSD physical maximum. Short windows and 120-second mean differ sharply. Repeated block contents; no claim about physical NAND bytes.
